messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1769501123 - gen-error-rate-high - P2
incident-bot: Detected at 2026-03-15T17:12:03Z. Condition: /v1/generate error rate > 2% sustained for 5m. Current: 3.8%. Paging oncall. Ticket: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-3421

Maya Patel: I'm on it, looking at the generation cluster now. First pass: looks like a client-side surge causing backend timeouts on one replica pool.

Liam O'Connor: Are customers impacted? Any high-traffic customers hitting endpoints?

Maya Patel: Early checks: traffic spike from region-us-east, origin header shows a handful of API keys from the same org. Rate limit not exceeded; requests are getting 502 from model-worker.

Kevin Zhang: Jumping in. Can you paste the worker logs?

Maya Patel: Pasting clipped logs below (sanitized):
```
2026-03-15T17:08:21Z model-worker-12 ERROR model_exec.go:245 token_gen failed: kv-cache fill timeout
2026-03-15T17:08:21Z model-worker-12 WARN intake.go:98 upstream latency 1200ms
2026-03-15T17:09:03Z model-worker-07 ERROR oom: runtime.OOMKilled
```

Sofia Ruiz: OOM on a worker — could be noisy restarts triggering transient errors. Are autoscaler events correlated? Grafana shows a scaling cooldown around 17:09 that prevented pod spin-up. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/generation-overview?from=now-30m

Kevin Zhang: Good catch. Hypothesis: a spike in long-context requests exhausted memory, autoscaler throttled new pods due to rapid churn -> error cascade -> alert noise.

Maya Patel: Mitigation steps I'm doing now:
- Evicting the problematic pod pool (model-worker-07) from the rotation
- Temporarily increasing replica min to 6 for generation pool
- Adding a short-term pod restart policy tweak to avoid OOM loop.

Maya Patel: Commands executed:
```bash
kubectl cordon model-worker-07
kubectl delete pod model-worker-07 -n generation
kubectl scale deployment generation --replicas=6 -n generation
```

incident-bot: NOTE: On-call handoff protocol requires explicit handover message if you step off.

Maya Patel: I'm going to hand off once we stabilize. ETA ~20m. I'll leave notes here and update the incident ticket.

Liam O'Connor: Customer impact assessment: PD alert shows 12 errors across 3 customers in last 5m, one is a paying customer with 95th percentile failures ~15%. We should flag support.

Sofia Ruiz: I can open a support blip for the affected customer. Tagging: @support-team. Add summary and mitigation.

Kevin Zhang: Short-term alert tuning suggestions to reduce noise while we investigate:
- Squelch duplicate gen-error-rate-high alerts for 10m for the same replica pool.
- Raise the firing threshold from 2% -> 2.5% for the generation endpoint until runbook change is merged.
- Add a cooldown window for pod OOM flapping alarms to 5m.

Maya Patel: I agree with those. We should capture the changes as a temporary patch in the alerting layer and then follow-up with a permanent runbook update. I'll assign owners.

Kevin Zhang: I'll make the alert manager change now (temp). Command: `amtool silence gen-error-rate-high --duration=10m --comment "temp: reduce noise during incident INC-3421"`

Sofia Ruiz: I'll create RD ticket RD-3421 for postmortem and runbook updates, link dashboards and add playbook notes.

Maya Patel: Handoff: I'm logging off at 17:32 UTC. Kevin will take lead for next 2 hours. Kevin, please confirm you accept.

Kevin Zhang: I accept. I'll carry the pager and finish the runbook edits.

Kevin Zhang: Notes for the runbook update (to be added):
- Alert ID: gen-error-rate-high (prometheus rule: generation:errors:rate5m)
- Root cause: memory pressure from long-context requests on a subset of workers -> OOM -> restart loop -> autoscaler cooldown
- Immediate mitigations taken: cordon + delete pod, scale replicas to 6, temporary alert silences and threshold bump
- Permanent actions proposed: add request-length pre-filtering, increase default worker memory to X GiB, improve autoscaler behavior for rapid spikes
- Owners: Kevin Zhang (runbook edits + alert rule change), Sofia Ruiz (dashboard + support communication), Maya Patel (follow-up infra fixes)
- Follow-up ticket: RD-3421 (postmortem + testing plan)

Maya Patel: Runbook link for reference: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/generation/errors

Kevin Zhang: I'll add an "annotations" section in the runbook with: "2026-03-15 - INC-3421 - temp threshold -> 2.5%, temp silence 10m applied. Owner: Kevin Zhang. Follow-up RD-3421."

Sofia Ruiz: For dashboards: I'll add a panel showing per-replica OOM counts and a short-term alert that triggers when >=2 OOMs in 3m for the same replica set. Will add link to RD-3421.

Liam O'Connor: For post-incident monitoring, suggest adding an automated smoke check that runs post-scale to ensure new pods finish warmup within 60s. Put that in the Optimize backlog.

Kevin Zhang: All mitigations applied. Error rate returning to baseline (0.4%). Keeping temp alert tuning in place until postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1769501123 updated: state=stabilized, severity=P3 (downgraded).

Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. I'll write the initial incident timeline for RD-3421 and drop the note in #postmortems once Kevin/Sofia add their pieces.

Kevin Zhang: Will update the runbook and link the alert rule PR. ETA for runbook PR: today EOD.

Sofia Ruiz: Support blip sent. Customer notified and offered workaround.

Liam O'Connor: Closing notes: remember to revert the temp threshold bump after runbook changes are in and tested. Add a checklist item for that in the RD-3421 story.

Kevin Zhang: Confirmed — will reopen this thread in 24h to validate reversion and ensure no regression.

Maya Patel: Handing off complete. Leaving incident notes and status in the ticket. Good job team :thumbsup:

Kevin Zhang: Acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring.
